subject: general
question: What type of pronoun is the word “This” in the sentence, “This is why habits are the compound interest of self-improvement." ?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"This"** is used to point to or indicate a specific idea or concept mentioned earlier in the passage.
 
• It replaces the previous explanation about how small daily habits compound over time to produce significant outcomes.
 
• Demonstrative pronouns are used to indicate specific things or ideas and include words like **this, that, these, those**. (संकेतात्मक सर्वनाम)
 
• **Example:** This is my favorite book among all the novels I have read.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Demonstrative pronoun**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflexive pronoun** (स्वयं-संबंधी सर्वनाम): Refers back to the subject of the sentence, e.g., "He taught himself." (उदाहरण: उसने स्वयं को पढ़ाया।)
 
• **Abstract pronoun** (अव्यक्त सर्वनाम): Not a standard grammatical category; pronouns do not generally get classified as abstract.
 
• **Subjective pronoun** (कर्तृवाचक सर्वनाम): Pronouns used as the subject of a sentence, e.g., "She runs every morning." (उदाहरण: वह हर सुबह दौड़ती है।)

137:Ta15,
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
